Key variables that could alter the outcome include revisions in official observations from Jeddah’s primary weather station, unexpected increases in humidity or wind that moderate peak heating, or late-day convective activity not currently indicated. Updated National Meteorological Center guidance or real-time station data remain the primary near-term catalysts.

title: Highest temperature in Cape Town on September 7?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Cape Town International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=fact

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:

Official National Weather Service forecasts and station observations indicate a mostly sunny to partly cloudy day with light variable winds shifting southerly, supporting temperatures climbing into the mid-90s before any isolated afternoon convection develops. Heat indices are projected to reach 105–107°F under high humidity typical of the region’s subtropical late-summer pattern. 

Recent climatological data show an average September 7 high near 91°F, with yesterday’s observed maximum of 91°F providing a baseline; today’s clearer skies and minimal cloud cover have allowed readings to trend toward the upper end of the forecast envelope. Model guidance shows limited spread, with no incoming fronts or tropical influences to suppress daytime heating. 

Resolution hinges on the official highest reported temperature at primary Houston stations (e.g., Hobby Airport), where afternoon peaks before 4–5 pm local time will determine the final bin. The market’s tight clustering around 92–95°F reflects this narrow uncertainty range in current observational and forecast data.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Minister Pistarini Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=saez

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from Argentina’s National Meteorological Service and supporting model runs indicate a daytime maximum of 13–14 °C for Buenos Aires on September 7 under stable northeast flow, clear to partly cloudy skies, and dry conditions following a cold weekend. Hourly data show temperatures climbing from morning lows near 5 °C to afternoon peaks of 12–13 °C, aligning with the market’s 94 % implied probability for a 13 °C high. This consensus reflects climatological norms for early September and the absence of warm advection or strong solar heating. A modest upward revision could occur only if local observations exceed model guidance due to urban heat-island effects or if later model runs shift the peak higher, though current data make such outcomes unlikely before the day concludes.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models and official outlooks from Singapore’s Meteorological Service and NEA indicate a partly cloudy day on September 8 with southeasterly winds and limited shower activity, supporting a daily maximum near 33°C.** Dry southwest monsoon conditions persisting across the region have reduced cloud cover and rainfall compared with typical September patterns, allowing stronger daytime heating while humidity remains high. Multiple numerical weather prediction runs cluster afternoon temperatures in the low-to-mid 30s Celsius, with 34°C possible only if skies clear more than expected. The 33°C outcome dominates market-implied odds because recent model consensus and the fortnight outlook’s 33–35°C range align closely with this value, while lower or higher thresholds require notable forecast shifts in the final model runs before the day begins.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Buckley Space Force Base Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kbkf

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts and supporting model guidance position a daily high of 85–87°F as the most likely outcome for Denver on September 8, driving the 46.5% market-implied odds on 86–87°F and 26% on 84–85°F. Mostly sunny skies after morning clouds, light easterly winds, and only isolated thunderstorm chances should allow temperatures to peak in that range under typical September insolation at Denver’s elevation. Recent observations show a modest cooling trend from early-September highs near 92–94°F, consistent with the current steering pattern. Trader consensus aligns closely with this guidance while assigning lower probability to 88°F-plus outcomes that would require stronger subsidence or clearer conditions than currently projected. Afternoon model updates remain the key near-term variable.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model runs point to rapid warming across Los Angeles on September 8 following the passage of moisture from Hurricane Marie’s remnants, with high pressure building and onshore flow weakening. Coastal stations such as LAX are forecast near 84°F while downtown and valley locations trend 90–96°F, reflecting the classic marine-layer suppression and compressional warming under the strengthening ridge. Trader consensus clusters tightly on 84–87°F because small differences in afternoon wind direction, residual low-level moisture, and exact clearing timing can shift the daily maximum by 2–3°F. Historical September averages near 76–77°F underscore how anomalous the post-Labor Day pattern remains, with resolution hinging on official observations at the designated station once the day ends.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest numerical weather prediction models, including runs from ECMWF and GFS, show northeasterly flow and increased cloud cover cooling Jinan on September 8 to a high near 23–25°C, down from 31–33°C the prior day. This stems from a regional pressure gradient favoring onshore winds that limit daytime heating, with consensus high temperatures clustered in that range across sources like AccuWeather and local forecasts. Trader-implied odds align closely with these outputs, assigning the highest probabilities to 23°C and 24°C while discounting 26°C or above. Inherent model uncertainty around exact cloud thickness and wind speeds leaves room for a 1–2°C shift by resolution, with updated guidance expected overnight.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from models including GFS and ECMWF place Taipei's September 9 maximum near 29–31 °C, consistent with the market's tight clustering around those outcomes. Subtropical high pressure and a strengthening northeast monsoon flow are expected to limit insolation through increased low-level cloud and scattered showers, while high humidity and urban heat retention in the basin moderate diurnal warming. Minor differences in boundary-layer moisture and wind timing among runs create the observed 1–2 °C spread; updated model cycles and afternoon observations on September 8 will likely narrow the range before resolution. Historical September highs average 30–31 °C, providing context for the current trader-implied distribution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Malaysian Meteorological Department and ensemble models position 32–34°C as the most likely peak range for Kuala Lumpur on September 9, with 33°C carrying the highest market-implied probability at 39%. Persistent haze from regional biomass burning, combined with increasing afternoon thunderstorm activity and cloud cover, is limiting daytime solar heating and suppressing temperatures below recent seasonal averages near 33°C. Light southwesterly winds and high humidity further moderate extremes, though any delay in convective development could allow brief spikes toward 34°C. Traders are monitoring updated model runs and official briefings ahead of the 48-hour forecast window, as shifts in storm timing or haze density remain the key variables that could alter the current consensus.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent National Weather Service and private forecasts converge on a Wednesday, September 9 high near 91 °F for Houston, with showers and thunderstorms likely after midday.** This pattern—driven by easterly flow, high humidity, and afternoon sea-breeze or convective activity—typically limits peak temperatures by increasing cloud cover and evaporative cooling once storms develop. Current model guidance and local office products place the most probable outcome in the lower 90s, aligning closely with the market’s leading 90-91 °F bin (39.5 % implied probability) and the secondary 88-89 °F and 92-93 °F ranges.

September climatology shows an average daily high of roughly 90.5 °F, so the forecast reflects near-normal conditions rather than an anomalous heat surge. Recent days have featured mid-90s readings under partly sunny skies with lower storm coverage; the shift toward higher PoP (30–70 %) on the 9th is the key near-term catalyst keeping probabilities centered on 90-91 °F. Traders appear to be weighting the risk that stronger or earlier convection could shave a degree or two versus the chance that delayed storms allow a brief push into the low 90s.

No major model disagreements or sudden pattern changes have emerged in the last 24–48 hours. Updated NWS Houston/Galveston guidance and ensemble output through early September 7 continue to support the current consensus, with resolution hinging on the exact timing and coverage of afternoon convection on the 9th.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent wet-season conditions in Panama City, with frequent afternoon convection and high humidity, are the main factors shaping trader views on the September 9 daily maximum.** 

September climatology shows typical highs near 30–31 °C, but heavy cloud build-up and scattered thunderstorms—driven by strong diurnal heating over warm Caribbean waters—often cap peaks by limiting solar insolation and triggering evaporative cooling. Recent model guidance points to 28–29 °C, yet the market’s clustering around 31–33 °C reflects uncertainty in exact storm timing and coverage. A later or weaker convective outbreak, lighter winds, or reduced moisture could allow brief clearing and push readings 1–2 °C higher, while earlier or more widespread rain would favor the lower side of the distribution. Updated short-range model runs and local observations over the next 48 hours will be the key catalysts for any shift in implied probabilities.
